origin.summary: Fix the placement, naming and authority boundary for Requirement bodies, candidates, Decisions, Evidence and schemas before structuring the added 13 Requirements.
origin.authorized_action: add this preparation step to Work 3 and prepare a decision candidate
not_yet_authorized: structure or promote the added 13 Requirements

problem.observed: Existing Requirement documents and records have usable content but no single rule fixes the separate locations and authority relations of bodies, candidate manifests, Decisions, Evidence and schemas.
problem.risk: A new structured record could appear current merely because of its path or filename, or a Decision could approve content other than the record later consumed.
problem.stop_boundary: Do not structure or promote the added 13 Requirements until this layout and authority rule has a Human Decision.

proposed_layout.role: Human-readable source, rationale or projection. Its directory does not make it normative.
Immutable machine-readable Requirement body. Effective authority is resolved externally.
Proposes an exact set of Requirement definition IDs, versions and digests for one Human judgment.
Records Human approval, rejection, revision request, supersession or revocation against exact target and Evidence digests.
Stores validation, review, coverage, post-write verification and migration observations without making the Requirement authoritative.
Machine authority for record shape and closed values, not for Requirement acceptance truth.
Lists the exact effective Requirement definitions and their approval Decisions. It is a derived authority map and cannot self-approve.

global_naming_rules: Embedded IDs are canonical; filenames and directories are locators and classification aids only.
Canonical filenames use lowercase ASCII IDs, two hyphens before a version, and no spaces.
Requirement IDs keep the REQ-<FEATURE>-<NNN> form; record_id is <requirement_id>@v<requirement_version>.
A referenced artifact is never renamed or edited in place; a changed artifact receives a new version or a new ID and an explicit supersedes relation.
Digest algorithm is SHA-256 until an approved migration changes it; every reference records path, logical ID, version and digest.
Timestamps are metadata and never replace ID, version or digest identity.

version_rules.requirement_version: Positive integer that increments for every new immutable Requirement definition record. acceptance_truth_changed states whether the revision changes obligation, stop, recovery, acceptance or non-goal truth.
version_rules.candidate_version: Positive integer scoped to candidate_id; any definition, schema, source or scope change creates a new candidate version and digest.
version_rules.schema_version: Positive integer scoped to schema_id. Existing records retain their recorded schema identity until an approved migration.
version_rules.evidence_version: New observation or rerun creates a new Evidence version; prior Evidence is retained and may become stale.
version_rules.decision_version: Decisions are immutable. Correction, supersession or revocation creates a new decision_id and typed relation.
version_rules.bundle_version: Any change to effective definitions, Decisions or legacy bindings creates a new authority bundle version.

effective_only_when: the Requirement definition validates against its recorded schema ID, version and digest
an immutable candidate manifest lists the exact definition ID, version and digest
a valid Human requirements_promotion Decision approves the exact candidate and Evidence digests
an authority bundle lists the definition and Decision references without duplicate ID and version conflicts
no later valid Decision supersedes or revokes the approval
required source, schema and Evidence bindings are not stale
never_sufficient: being stored under docs/requirements, records/requirements or a directory named current or approved
having an approved-looking filename or embedded status without a valid Decision
a Decision that names an ID but omits the target version or digest
an Evidence pass result without a promotion Decision
authority_resolution.conflict_result: authority_inconsistent; stop promotion and downstream compilation

stale_rules.change: Requirement definition ID, version or digest changes
stales: candidate validation for the prior target
review and Evidence that claim the new target
Decision reuse for the new target
downstream Contract or Verification compiled from the prior target
stale_rules.recovery: Create a new candidate, rerun affected validation and review, obtain a new Human Decision, and issue a new authority bundle.

stale_rules.change: Schema meaning or closed values change
stale_rules.recovery: Retain old records under their recorded schema, define compatibility and migration, validate representative positive, negative and boundary records, then obtain a migration Decision.

stale_rules.change: Fixed source or human-readable source changes
stale_rules.recovery: Capture the new source digest, classify semantic effect, and rerun affected coverage and authority checks.

stales: authority bundle entries that rely on it
downstream unexecuted permits or promotion claims
stale_rules.recovery: Create a new Decision and authority bundle, then recompute downstream stale closure.

stale_rules.change: Only the locator path changes while ID, version and content digest remain identical
stale_rules.recovery: Issue a new locator or authority-bundle version and recheck references; do not infer a semantic Requirement change.

legacy_migration.current_rule: Do not move or rewrite the existing 37 Requirement documents and records in this Work.
legacy_migration.binding: Treat the existing stage-four approval, completion and fixed source digests as explicit legacy_authority_bindings.
legacy_migration.added_13_rule: Create the added 13 structured definitions only after this layout candidate is approved and the minimum schema is fixed.
legacy_migration.mixed_bundle_rule: Before the 50-Requirement set becomes effective, issue one authority bundle that lists the 37 legacy bindings and the 13 new definition, Decision and digest bindings.
legacy_migration.future_migration: Migration of the 37 legacy Requirements into the new definition format is a separate candidate, validation, Decision and stale-closure Work Item.

implementation_sequence_after_approval: create only the approved directories and a short non-authoritative README explaining locator roles
create and validate the minimum Requirement definition, candidate, Decision, Evidence and authority-bundle schemas
create an explicit legacy binding inventory for the existing 37 Requirements
structure the added 13 Requirements as immutable definitions
build and audit the 50-Requirement authority bundle
request a separate Human promotion Decision for the structured Requirements
out_of_scope: moving or rewriting existing Requirement artifacts before a migration Decision
approving or structuring the added 13 Requirements in this candidate
creating a generic artifact registry or plugin system
making directory names or symlinks authority
changing the current Plan or Requirement acceptance truth
approved_effect: none until a Human Decision is bound to this candidate digest
